# @QB_NAME@ — a qb actor-framework project.
#
# Generated by qb-new-project.sh from isndev/qb-sample-project (@QB_TEMPLATE_REF@),
# against qb @QB_VERSION@.
#
# ---------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------
# HOW qb GETS HERE, AND WHY IT IS NOT A SUBMODULE
# ---------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------
# FetchContent, at a ref the scaffolder wrote into this file when it generated the project.
#
# The template this came from used to carry qb as a git submodule, and the gitlink it stored went
# two major versions stale without anything noticing — the template still built, against a qb from
# before v2.0.0. A dependency pinned INSIDE a template can only ever drift away from the qb whose
# script cloned it. Deciding the ref at scaffold time instead makes that impossible: the version
# comes from the qb the script shipped with, so fetching the one-liner from a tag pins that
# release and fetching it from a branch follows that line.
#
# The practical difference for you: no `git submodule update --init --recursive`, and no detached
# submodule HEADs in your history. `cmake -S . -B build` is the whole setup.
#
# WORKING ON qb ITSELF? Point CMake at your own checkout — no edit to this file:
#     cmake -S . -B build -DFETCHCONTENT_SOURCE_DIR_QB=/path/to/qb
# The same works per module: FETCHCONTENT_SOURCE_DIR_QBM-HTTP, ..._QBM-PGSQL, ..._QBM-REDIS.
# CMake then skips the download entirely and builds your tree in place.
#
# PINNING FOR PRODUCTION. QB_GIT_REF below is what the scaffolder resolved on the day you ran it.
# If it names a branch, you are following a moving line: set it to a released tag (or a commit
# sha, dropping GIT_SHALLOW) once you want reproducible builds.
# ---------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------

cmake_minimum_required(VERSION 3.24)

project(@QB_NAME@
        VERSION 0.1.0
        DESCRIPTION "A qb actor-framework project"
        LANGUAGES CXX)

set(QB_GIT_REF "@QB_REF@" CACHE STRING
    "The isndev/qb (and qbm module) git ref this project builds against")

option(@QB_NAME_UPPER@_BUILD_TESTS "Build the ${PROJECT_NAME} test suite" OFF)

# Which qbm modules to fetch. Trim this to what you use: each one is a clone at configure time
# and a static library at build time. `http` alone is the common case.
set(@QB_NAME_UPPER@_MODULES http pgsql redis CACHE STRING
    "qbm modules to fetch and link (subset of: http pgsql redis)")

# -----------------------------------------------------------------------------
# Dependencies
# -----------------------------------------------------------------------------
include(FetchContent)

# qb's own build policy, decided HERE and never inherited from this project's test option.
#
# The obvious wiring — QB_BUILD_TESTS follows @QB_NAME_UPPER@_BUILD_TESTS — was tried and is
# wrong, and the numbers are why. QB_BUILD_TESTS is global: turning it on to get YOUR two tests
# also registers qb's and every fetched module's, measured at 176 ctest entries and 534 build
# targets for a project that owns 2 of them. `cmake --build build` would then compile the
# framework's entire test suite, and a bare `ctest` would try to RUN it.
#
# So the dependencies are always built without their tests, and this project registers its own
# directly in tests/CMakeLists.txt — with the same target names and labels qb_add_test() would
# have produced, because the convention is worth keeping even where the helper is not usable
# (it early-returns unless QB_BUILD_TESTS is ON, which is exactly what must stay off).
set(QB_BUILD_TESTS OFF CACHE BOOL "" FORCE)
set(QB_BUILD_BENCHMARKS OFF CACHE BOOL "" FORCE)
set(QB_BUILD_EXAMPLES OFF CACHE BOOL "" FORCE)
# This is a source super-build, never an install target: qb's install(EXPORT) rules must not run
# here (with a source-built zlib they are a hard generate error, not a warning).
set(QB_INSTALL OFF CACHE BOOL "" FORCE)
set(QBM_INSTALL OFF CACHE BOOL "" FORCE)

# Position-independent code for the whole tree. qb sets it for its own subtree, but the qbm
# modules and their bundled static dependencies are added from THIS scope, so it is set here too.
set(CMAKE_POSITION_INDEPENDENT_CODE ON)

FetchContent_Declare(qb
        GIT_REPOSITORY https://github.com/isndev/qb.git
        GIT_TAG        ${QB_GIT_REF}
        GIT_SHALLOW    TRUE)
FetchContent_MakeAvailable(qb)

# qb must be available before any module: a qbm CMakeLists.txt calls qb_register_module(), which
# is defined by qb/cmake/qbFunctions.cmake. It says so with a FATAL_ERROR rather than dying on
# whichever qb_* command it reaches first, so getting the order wrong is loud, not mysterious.
foreach(_mod IN LISTS @QB_NAME_UPPER@_MODULES)
    FetchContent_Declare(qbm-${_mod}
            GIT_REPOSITORY https://github.com/isndev/qbm-${_mod}.git
            GIT_TAG        ${QB_GIT_REF}
            GIT_SHALLOW    TRUE)
endforeach()
if(@QB_NAME_UPPER@_MODULES)
    list(TRANSFORM @QB_NAME_UPPER@_MODULES PREPEND "qbm-" OUTPUT_VARIABLE _module_targets)
    FetchContent_MakeAvailable(${_module_targets})
endif()

# YOUR OWN MODULES. Anything under qbm/ is loaded from source — that is where a module scaffolded
# with qb-new-module.sh goes, and it is exposed as qbm::<name> exactly like the official ones:
#     cd qbm && curl -fsSL .../qb-new-module.sh | bash /dev/stdin mymodule
# Guarded by IS_DIRECTORY because qb_load_modules() treats a missing directory as an error, and an
# empty qbm/ is the normal state of a new project.
if(IS_DIRECTORY "${CMAKE_CURRENT_SOURCE_DIR}/qbm")
    qb_load_modules("${CMAKE_CURRENT_SOURCE_DIR}/qbm")
endif()

get_property(_loaded_modules GLOBAL PROPERTY QB_MODULE_LIBRARIES)
qb_status_message("[@QB_NAME@] qb ${QB_FRAMEWORK_VERSION} @ ${QB_GIT_REF}, modules: ${_loaded_modules}")

# -----------------------------------------------------------------------------
# The project
# -----------------------------------------------------------------------------
# Application logic lives in a library, not in main.cpp, so that the test suite can link exactly
# what ships. A test that reaches its subject through a second copy of the source is testing a
# copy. main.cpp stays thin on purpose: argument parsing and engine startup, nothing else.
add_library(@QB_NAME@-lib STATIC
        src/app/greeting.cpp)
target_include_directories(@QB_NAME@-lib PUBLIC "${CMAKE_CURRENT_SOURCE_DIR}/src")
target_link_libraries(@QB_NAME@-lib PUBLIC qb::core qb::io)
target_compile_features(@QB_NAME@-lib PUBLIC cxx_std_20)

# The version string the binary reports, composed from project(VERSION) above. Do not write it
# out a second time in C++: two copies of a version are two chances to disagree, and every stale
# version string this project has fixed started as a well-intentioned literal.
target_compile_definitions(@QB_NAME@-lib PUBLIC @QB_NAME_UPPER@_VERSION="${PROJECT_VERSION}")

# src/app/api_actor.h is an HTTP server, so the module is a hard requirement rather than an
# optional extra. Said here, at configure time, instead of as a wall of template errors.
if(NOT TARGET qbm::http)
    message(FATAL_ERROR
        "@QB_NAME@ links qbm::http, but 'http' is not in @QB_NAME_UPPER@_MODULES "
        "(currently: ${@QB_NAME_UPPER@_MODULES}). Either keep it, or drop src/app/api_actor.h "
        "and the ApiActor lines in src/main.cpp.")
endif()
target_link_libraries(@QB_NAME@-lib PUBLIC qbm::http)

add_executable(@QB_NAME@ src/main.cpp)
target_link_libraries(@QB_NAME@ PRIVATE @QB_NAME@-lib)

# A predictable path, so the README, the CI workflow and you all name the same file.
set_target_properties(@QB_NAME@ PROPERTIES
        RUNTIME_OUTPUT_DIRECTORY "${CMAKE_BINARY_DIR}/bin")

# -----------------------------------------------------------------------------
# Tests
# -----------------------------------------------------------------------------
if(@QB_NAME_UPPER@_BUILD_TESTS)
    # GoogleTest at the version qb itself pins. Read from qb's cache variable rather than
    # written out again here: a second version literal is a second thing to keep in step, and
    # every stale version this ecosystem has had to fix began as one.
    FetchContent_Declare(googletest
            GIT_REPOSITORY https://github.com/google/googletest.git
            GIT_TAG        ${QB_GOOGLETEST_GIT_TAG}
            GIT_SHALLOW    TRUE)
    set(gtest_force_shared_crt ON CACHE BOOL "" FORCE)
    FetchContent_MakeAvailable(googletest)

    enable_testing()
    add_subdirectory(tests)
endif()
